chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Zakkar ibn Farqad, from 'Uthman ibn Ziyad — he said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): 'I am on a journey and I come upon the pooled stagnant water (al-naqee'), and my hand is unclean, and I plunge it into the water.' He said: 'No harm (lā ba's).'
The intended meaning [of this hadith] is [that it applies] when the water has reached the measure of the kurr, which does not accept [ritual] impurity — and what clarifies that [follows].

key_terms.اَلْكُرِّ: kurr — the minimum water volume (approx. 377 litres in Shia fiqh) that renders water immune to ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to plunge an unclean hand into pooled stagnant water while traveling according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith records 'Uthman ibn Ziyad asking Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) whether plunging an unclean hand into pooled stagnant water (al-naqee') while traveling is permissible, to which the Imam replied 'lā ba's' (no harm). Shaykh al-Tusi qualifies this ruling, explaining it applies only when the water has reached the volume of a kurr — the minimum measure at which water becomes immune to ritual contamination by najasah.
